author: Mike Shaughnessy
title: Eagan finishes 2nd in Sub-State Legion tourney - NewsBreak
text: Two losses to Hastings end Patriots’ season The Eagan American Legion Baseball team lost only five games all summer, but two of the losses came at the worst possible time for the Patriots. Hastings defeated Eagan 5-3 on Monday night at Big Goat Field to win the Sub-State 6 tournament and a place in this week’s state Senior American Legion tournament in St. Michael. Hastings also defeated Eagan 6-5 on Sunday to force Monday’s deciding game. The Patriots (16-5) had won eight consecutive games, including a 10-0 victory over Hastings earlier in the Sub-State tourney, before losing their last two. Hastings took a 5-2 lead in Monday’s game with a four-run fifth inning that included a run-scoring single, two-run single, and another run scoring on an error. The Patriots responded in the bottom of the inning with an RBI single by Jacob Bjorkstrand. Eagan had the potential tying run on base in the bottom of the seventh before Hastings got out of the inning. Outfielder Drew Boyd had three hits and scored a run for the Patriots. Eagan was unbeaten in the double-elimination Sub-State tournament when it played Hastings on Sunday. The Patriots appeared to be on their way to the state tournament after holding a 5-0 lead after four innings. But Hastings stormed back in the sixth. Its first five batters reached base on four singles and a double. That cut Eagan’s lead to 5-3. A one-out single scored Hastings’ fourth run, and the final two runs of the inning came in on an error. Eagan put a runner in scoring position in each of the final two innings but could not get him around. Boyd was 2-for-4 with two runs and two RBIs for Eagan. Tate Gage was 2-for-4 with one RBI. The Patriots started the Sub-State tournament with an 11-1 victory over East Ridge on July 24. Tyler Wigley was 3-for-3 with one RBI and one run scored. Boyd’s bases-loaded triple ended the game by the 10-run rule in the fifth inning. Dylan Wilcox also drove in three runs. Bjorkstrand scored on a wild pitch in the bottom of the seventh as Eagan defeated Woodbury Blue 7-6 in the second round. Bjorkstrand led off the inning with a single, stole second and advanced to third on a groundout. Infielder Theo King had two hits and two RBIs for the Patriots. Camden Sexton pitched a five-inning one-hit shutout as Eagan routed Hastings 10-0 in the third round July 26. Gage and Mitch Young drove in two runs each. A furious seventh-inning rally gave Eagan a 6-5 victory over Bayport on Sunday and sent the Patriots to the Sub-State finals. Trailing 5-1, Eagan got consecutive singles from King, Boyd and Bjorkstrand, with King scoring on Bjorkstrand’s hit. Gage reached on an error, loading the bases, and Young’s two-run single cut the Bayport lead to 5-4. Wigley walked, re-loading the bases. Tony Hyvare’s sacrifice fly scored Gage with the tying run. Two batters later, Young scored from third on a wild pitch. Eastview Eastview Thunder Black went 1-2 in the Sub-State 6 tournament, losing to Hastings 6-0 in the first round and defeating Inver Grove Heights 12-10 in the elimination bracket before falling to Woodbury Blue 10-6. The Thunder finished their season 7-13. Outfielder Pablo Torcat-Elorza was 2-for-3 with three RBIs in the Inver Grove Heights game, where Eastview took a 7-0 lead in the first inning before holding off an IGH comeback. Infielder Armen Mcketarian was 2-for-2 with two runs and one RBI, and infielder Ben Schmitz drove in two runs. Torcat-Elorza had three hits and Mcketarian, Liam Soderlund and Jayden Bonine had two each in the Woodbury Blue game. Mike Shaughnessy can be reached at mike.shaughnessy@apgecm.com.
